title: Minimum Operations to Equalize Subarrays
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, you can perform operations where each operation involves increasing or decreasing any element of nums by exactly k.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, you can perform operations where each operation involves increasing or decreasing any element of nums by exactly k. For each query defined by [li, ri] in a 2D integer array queries, calculate the minimum number of operations required to make all elements in the subarray nums[li..ri] equal. If it is impossible to make all elements equal with the given operations, the answer for that query is -1. Return an array ans where ans[i] corresponds to the answer for the ith query.
constraints: nums and queries each contain up to 40,000 entries and k is positive.
One operation changes one value by exactly +k or -k.
For each inclusive query, return minimum operations to equalize its values, or negative one if impossible.
hints: Values can meet only when all have the same remainder modulo k; then divide away k and minimize unit moves.
A prefix count of adjacent remainder changes tests feasibility for each range.
Persistent order-statistic trees find the range median and prefix count/sum, which give total absolute deviation.
The median minimizes absolute distance, and persistent root differences represent exactly the queried subarray.
editorial: The median minimizes absolute distance, and persistent root differences represent exactly the queried subarray.

tests.explanation: Normalized values 0,1,2 require one and two median moves.
Mixed residues make the first query impossible; the others cost zero and one.
